data.title: Free parking at train stations, malls in flooded Bangkok
data.description: Many buildings around Bangkok and surrounding areas are offering free parking for people affected by flooding, including park-and-ride facilities at train stations and garages at shopping malls.

data.title: Northern property market slows new launches as Chiang Mai faces four-year stock overhang
data.description: Northern Thailand’s housing market is recovering gradually, but weak purchasing power and tight lending are slowing new launches, while Chiang Mai may need more than four years to clear existing stock.

data.title: Man City to appeal serious Premier League charges

data.title: Nepal tunnel survivor wants to help post-flood rebuild
data.description: KIRTIPUR , Nepal - Pulled alive 10 days after catastrophic floods trapped him in a tunnel, Nepali hydropower worker Kabir Maharjan is determined to help rebuild his country despite his own harrowing ordeal.

data.title: Indonesia fires threaten critically endangered orangutans
data.description: JAKARTA - Wildfires that tore through Indonesian Borneo's vast tropical forests have piled pressure on critically endangered Bornean orangutans, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) said on Saturday.

data.title: All 50 Bangkok districts declared disaster areas
data.description: All 50 districts of Bangkok have been declared disaster zones as heavy rain continues to cause flooding, traffic problems and disruptions to daily life.

data.title: Reclaiming private space
data.description: In A Room Of One's Own (1929), Virginia Woolf argued that women must have money and space to write fiction. A century later, a group of theatre artists expand the thesis of their predecessor's feminist polemic. Despite enjoying access to the material basis for creative pursuit, women nowadays are still excluded from their most private space -- their bodies -- and subject to patriarchal domination.

data.title: Democrats face identity test

data.title: Hudson hails his 'best ever' War Elephants
data.description: Thailand begin their quest for Fifa Asean Cup glory in Bandung today, with head coach Anthony Hudson declaring he has never enjoyed working with a squad more as his side prepared to open their campaign against Pakistan.

data.title: EPL delivers another dose of drama and keeps the fans guessing
data.description: Due to the extended international break, there are no Premier League games for a couple of weeks. However, EPL fans can savour last weekend's action, in which the league gave us a reminder of its capacity to provide upsets and entertainment.

data.title: Port say bye to Sarawut, get Bandovic
data.description: Port FC have ended their relationship with head coach Sarawut Treephan by mutual consent, the Thai League 1 club announced yesterday, bringing to a close a decade-long association that yielded some of the most significant silverware in the club's recent history.

data.title: Amlo to take victims' claims
data.description: The Anti-Money Laundering Office (Amlo) is preparing to accept claims from victims of alleged investment fraud involving Yim Leak, Benjamin Mauerberger, also known as Ben Smith, and their associates. data.title: BMTA sees EV fleet as ticket to ending losses
data.description: The Bangkok Mass Transit Authority (BMTA) expects to end its operating losses by 2030 as an electric vehicle (EV) fleet cuts costs and raises efficiency.

It is a translation of the battles of ideas, planning and decision-making, which culminated in the borderlines that have come to define the particular territories in which some communities had to settle, with or without choice.

data.title: Vegetarian Festival in Phuket to net 1.4 billion baht

data.title: Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
